title: dynamic-fallback-switchboard-for-kernel-compatibility-and-kv-safety
author: Carlos M. Rivera
release_notes: Introduces a dynamic fallback switchboard to safely route requests between optimized kernels and compatibility kernels when KV cache or kernel probes indicate risk. Default behavior is backward compatible; admins can tune soft-thresholds and escalation policies via runtime config.
description: Motivation: we observed intermittent correctness regressions when speculative fast-path kernel swaps coincided with KV-cache miss storms and non-idempotent attention kernels. This PR adds a lightweight 'switchboard' abstraction that centralizes safety checks, soft-threshold gating, and staged fallback escalation so we can keep the fast path available for steady-state traffic while minimizing correctness incidents during transient stress. Design: - Switchboard maintains a small compatibility matrix keyed by (model-arch, kernel-variant, quant-mode) and a per-route risk score derived from KV miss-rate, recent kernel error rates, and latency variance. - Soft thresholds: two levels (warn, escalate). Warn logs metrics and reduces batch aggressiveness; escalate forces deterministic compatibility kernel and freezes KV-prefetch until risk subsides. - Burst-padding: short-lived padding of batch size for routes that saw a sudden drop in throughput to avoid tiny batches that exacerbate latency spikes. - Compatibility probes: speculative probes run on a sampled fraction of requests to validate parity between optimized and compatibility kernels; probe windows decay to avoid excess CPU during sustained risk. - Config: runtime config via /config/runtime.json and feature flags (SAFE_FALLBACK_PERCENT, PROBE_SAMPLING_RATE, RISK_DECAY_SEC). No schema changes to public API. Developer notes: The switchboard is implemented in src/runtime/switchboard.cc and is integrated as a pluggable policy for scheduler::ContinuousBatcher and for the kernel selection path in src/runtime/kernel_selector.cc. KV safety hooks were added in src/kv/cache_manager.cc to report miss streaks and cold-start indicators. The change includes a small compatibility matrix in configs/compat-matrix.yaml and a doc summary in docs/compatibility/switchboard.md. Tests: unit tests for switchboard logic (tests/switchboard_test.cc), integration test for correctness under simultaneous KV miss and kernel swap (tests/integration/kv_kernel_stress_test.py). Benchmarks: microbench harness shows 0.8% median latency regression for p95-sensitive routes when switchboard is enabled in conservative mode, with a 12% reduction in correctness incidents on stress fixtures. Rollout: feature-flagged rollout with gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and canary that enables escalate path only in lower-traffic regions for first 48 hours. Related: addresses ENG-8472 (reduce correctness regressions from speculative kernels) and provides mitigations requested in SUP-4123 (customer incident). Checklist: [x] design docs updated [x] unit/integration tests [x] metrics and dashboards [x] feature-flag gating [x] release notes

patch_snippets:
// switchboard: lightweight risk score -> 0..1
float evaluate_risk(const RiskWindow& w) { return min(1.0f, w.kv_miss_rate * 0.6f + w.kernel_err_rate * 0.4f + w.latency_cv * 0.2f); }

// kernel_selector: consult switchboard before commit
if (switchboard->should_escalate(route, current_state)) { select_compatibility_kernel(); } else { select_fast_kernel(); }
